rationale: bugs_open/429: the publish seam's b2worker backend (DGH-008, the hosted mirror every customer site serves from for its first 30 days) copies creates/updates and contains NO deletion handling, so a retracted page's hosted object serves 200 at the slug FOR EVER. Found live on the first paid site (boxingonline.com) minutes after the platform's first successful page retraction: every stage of the unpublish chain succeeded (page archived, nav cleared, git deleted, origin b2-synced --delete) and https://boxingonline.ugg2.com/contact.html still serves — re-verified today with controls (contact 200, sibling 200, invented URL 404). THE GUARANTEE CHANGE, STATED PLAINLY: the mirror becomes destructive at the destination — Publish now CONVERGES, deleting destination keys whose source key is gone, with the copy half's own verification discipline (sweep from the same destination listing the ETag verify uses; re-list; verify swept keys GONE), and publish_site's served-bytes acceptance becomes a PAIR when anything probe-worthy was swept (swept key must 404, kept .html must still 200, cache-busted, status codes only — byte-compares walk into the CDN-adds-bytes landmine; robots.txt excluded since the edge rewrites it to a 200, which would otherwise wedge the retry loop permanently). published_hash is written only after the pair passes, so failure leaves drift standing and the next tick retries an idempotent sweep. CONSUMERS, ENUMERATED NOT ASSERTED: SELECT domain FROM sites WHERE publish_target IS NOT NULL -> 2 rows (2026-09-02): boxingonline.com, noted.co.uk. Both owning lanes told directly (two-way exchange with the site_delivery_and_editor session, which filed the bug and holds the consumer-side close criterion; no veto — they contributed two of the guards below). SAFETY ANALYSIS (fail-danger asymmetry): a missed delete is fail-safe (drift stands, next tick retries). The dangerous direction is a source listing that lies short — so (1) storage.S3Client.ListObjects (s3.go:170) runs ListObjectsV2Paginator to exhaustion and a mid-page error aborts the WHOLE listing (fails loud, never partial); (2) an EMPTY file set is REFUSED outright in the backend (an empty source cannot license sweeping the mirror — whole-site teardown stays bugs_open/304's decision, and this refusal names it); (3) a bulk floor: a sweep removing >20 orphans AND >50% of the destination refuses without the new opt-in allow_bulk_unpublish input — default OFF, the 2026-08-02 section-2 shape, ZERO live consumers (the reconciler's shim dispatch maps only {site_id, domain}, verified in 422_site_publish_reconciler_HOLD.sql, so the scheduled path structurally cannot pass it); per RFC_022 this opt-in-default-OFF-zero-consumers field is NOT architecture-scope. Even a truncated listing that slipped under the floor is recoverable: the source is authoritative and untouched, the truncated tree's hash IS the drift, and the next full-listing tick republishes the wrongly-swept copies — bounded staleness, never data loss. ROLLOUT: TreeHash prefix th1->th2, algorithm unchanged. This is the prefix's designed purpose ('republishes once, explicably') and it is load-bearing here: the motivating orphan is INVISIBLE to drift (published_hash already reflects the post-retraction tree), so without the bump the fix would never fire on it. Post-roll both opted-in sites drift exactly once and converge via the normal hourly one-site-per-tick rotation — no migration, no forced ticks (the reconciler-force landmine). Zip deliverable keys carry only the last-12-hex sha tail, so zip naming is unaffected (delivery lane confirmed zero cost for the live order). FILES MENTIONED BUT ABSENT FROM THE EDIT LIST, ONE CLAUSE EACH: the DGH-008 register entry, a new LANDMINES entry (mirror now sweeps hand-placed objects; mass restructure needs a hand dispatch), appends to bugs_open/429 and bugs_open/304, and the bugfix_429_mirror_unpublish working docs are PROSE riding the same commit — refused client-side by the gate and deliberately not edits here. 422_site_publish_reconciler_HOLD.sql is cited as evidence only, unchanged. Tests are mutation-proven where a fake's bookkeeping cannot assert a negative: a Delete that silently no-ops must fail publish (proves the post-sweep re-list verify is live), the floor must refuse before deleting, and a swept key still serving 200 must provably NOT write published_hash.

edits.rationale: Delete joins the ObjectStore contract (compile-time — an optional interface would let a store degrade back into 429 silently; implementers enumerated: storage.S3Client already has Delete, plus the two package fakes). Request.AllowBulkUnpublish opt-in default OFF. Result carries Deleted/DeletedKeys for the caller's 404 acceptance. th2 prefix = the designed republish-once lever.

The deletion half: empty-set refusal, orphan sweep from the existing verify listing, bulk floor (>20 AND >50% without AllowBulkUnpublish), per-key delete, post-sweep re-list verification mirroring the copy half's discipline.
Fake gains Delete plus deleteSilentlyFails (the corruptKey discipline applied to the deletion half). Four new tests incl. the mutation proof that a silently-failing Delete cannot publish.
The pinned-prefix assertion moves th1->th2 in the same commit — without this the bump breaks shared HEAD (caught by adversarial pre-review, not by the author).

Plumbs allow_bulk_unpublish (4th optional key, well under the N=10 budget). Empty-tree skip reason now names the standing hosted copy when published_hash exists (no silent skip, no implicit delete-all). deletionAcceptance: the 404/200 pair before published_hash writes; recorded key list capped at 20 (results land in collected_data).
Action-level pair proof: sweep reaches the result and the 404 probe; a swept key still serving 200 fails acceptance and provably does NOT write published_hash (sqlmock, no ExpectExec).
